acceptanceCriteria: Both subtests pass 20 consecutive runs with -count=20 under a synthetic CPU load (for example stress or parallel go test) on darwin.
If the streaming timeout classification is wrong rather than the test, the fix keeps git-timeout only for a real deadline and the parity test covers it.
body: Suspected load flake (not yet reproduced in isolation). Observed in the V1-0414 full-gate run 2026-10-17 04:55-08:55 UTC (attempt e9a499d1, tree ddccd4d2, main 69c6cac03, Go 1.27.2, darwin, host load 30-60), gate output evidence sha256 b190b8be302c8bac1153c92130e70b79a5f24d595857715664eb0bf964693255. internal/cem/gitrun: stream_unix_test.go:38 'stream=git-timeout: Git operation timed out buffered=git-exit-failure: Git exited unsuccessfully: doom' (parity/exit expected matching codes; the streaming path classified a plain exit as timeout); stream_unix_test.go:84 'open .../grandchild: no such file or directory' in the cancellation subtest (the grandchild never wrote its marker before cancellation). Package FAIL in 7.7s. Expected: parity and descendant-containment hold regardless of host load, or the tests bound their timing assumptions. Actual: both fail under load.
